item.aggregated_output:
project:
  name: "RBI_MPC_In_Silico"
  version: "3.0.0-research-upgrade"

run:
  provider: "gemini"                      # "gemini" | "openai" | "anthropic" | "ollama" | "mock"
  dev_model: "gemini-3.1-flash-lite"
  final_model: "gemini-3.1-flash-lite"
  fallback_models: []                    # A different model is a separately frozen condition
  rate_limit_rpm: 5                       # Google AI Studio Free Tier limit is 5 RPM
  budget_usd_cap: 25.0
  temperature: 0.6
  n_replicates: 3
  seed_base: 42
  use_cache: true
  cache_dir: ".cache/llm_cache.sqlite"
  max_output_tokens: 2048
  request_timeout_seconds: 60
  model_epoch: "2026-10-05-standard-api"
  budget_ledger_path: ".cache/research_v3_budget.sqlite"

decision_space:
  action_set_bps: [-50, -25, 0, 25, 35, 40, 50]
  simulate_stance: true
  stance_set: ["withdrawal_of_accommodation", "neutral", "accommodative"]

panels:
  primary_roster: "2020_2024"
  primary_panel_start: "2020-10-01"
  primary_panel_end: "2024-08-31"
  calibration_holdout_split: 0.68         # Explicit historical split: 17 calibration / 8 exposed retrospective evaluation
  forward_test_panel_start: "2024-10-01"
  forward_test_panel_end: "latest"

taylor_rule:
  r_star_pct: 1.4
  pi_star_pct: 4.0
  hp_filter_lambda: 14400                 # Ravn-Uhlig monthly parameter
  smoothing_rho: 0.75                     # Interest rate inertia
  default_alpha: 1.5
  default_beta: 0.5
  default_gamma: 0.2                      # Open-economy US Fed Funds sensitivity
  us_neutral_rate_pct: 2.5

monte_carlo:
  n_draws: 1000
  macro_noise_std_pct: 0.20

validation:
  # Descriptive channel thresholds; empirical readiness requires separate evidence.
  directional_accuracy_threshold: 0.75
  stance_accuracy_threshold: 0.70

No model call, outcome-dependent fit, retrospective biography, or silent ontology
mapping occurs here.  Realized attendance remains an explicitly oracle input.

def sha256(payload):
    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()


def normalized(text):
    return " ".join(text.split())


def canonical_member_id(value):
    result = ALIAS.get(value, value)
    if result not in MEMBERS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown member identity: {value}")
    return result


def canonical_roster(values):
    result = tuple(canonical_member_id(value) for value in values)
    if len(result) != 6 or len(set(result)) != 6:
        raise ValueError("Alias normalization would duplicate or omit an attendee")
    return result


def _read_json(path):
    def unique(pairs):
        result = {}
        for key, value in pairs:
            if key in result:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate JSON key {key}")
            result[key] = value
        return result
    def reject(value):
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid JSON constant {value}")
    return json.loads(path.read_text(), object_pairs_hook=unique, parse_constant=reject)


def source_path(root, relative):
    path = (root / relative).resolve()
    if not path.is_relative_to(root) or not path.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f"Missing or outside-root scientific input: {relative}")
    return path


def _publication_day(soup):
    """Read retained RBI header only; never infer publication from decision day."""
    body = soup.select_one("#doublescroll")
    if body is None:
        return None
    matches = re.findall(r"Date\s*:\s*([A-Za-z]+\s+\d{1,2},\s*\d{4})",
                         normalized(body.get_text(" ", strip=True))[:300])
    if len(matches) != 1:
        return None
    for fmt in ("%b %d, %Y", "%B %d, %Y"):
        try:
            return datetime.strptime(matches[0], fmt).date().isoformat()
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return None


def _name_present(text, identifier):
    name = MEMBERS[identifier][0]
    # The original roster abbreviates Jayanth R. and Mridul K. inconsistently.
    if identifier == "jayanth_varma":
        return bool(re.search(r"Jayanth\s+(?:R\.?\s+)?Varma", text))
    if identifier == "mridul_saggar":
        return bool(re.search(r"Mridul\s+(?:K\.?\s+)?Saggar", text))
    return name in text


def _personal_heading(text, identifier):
    prefix = re.match(r"Statement\s+by\s+(.+?)(?=\s+\d+\.|$)", normalized(text))
    if prefix is None or not _name_present(prefix.group(0), identifier):
        raise ValueError(f"Personal attribution heading missing or wrong for {identifier}")
    return prefix.group(0)


class _SourceStore:
    def __init__(self, root):
        self.root = root
        self.inputs = {}
        self.payloads = {}
        self.origin_to_portable = {}
        self.soups = {}

    def read(self, relative, expected=None):
        path = source_path(self.root, relative)
        payload = path.read_bytes()
        digest = sha256(payload)
        if expected is not None and digest != expected:
            raise ValueError(f"Scientific input hash mismatch: {relative}")
        self.inputs[str(relative)] = digest
        portable = "sources/" + digest + path.suffix
        self.payloads[portable] = payload
        self.origin_to_portable[str(relative)] = portable
        return path, payload

    def ref(self, relative, expected, source_id, url, claimed_publication):
        _, payload = self.read(relative, expected)
        soup = BeautifulSoup(payload, "html.parser")
        publication = _publication_day(soup)
        # A missing header stays missing. A disagreement is corruption, not an
        # opportunity to prefer the ledger's date.
        if publication is not None and publication != claimed_publication:
            raise ValueError(f"Publication ledger/header mismatch for {relative}")
        self.soups[str(relative)] = soup
        return DatedSourceRef(
            source_id=source_id, source_file=str(relative), source_sha256=expected,
            source_url=url, publication_date=publication,
            publication_status="verified_retained_header" if publication else "unresolved")


def _roster(meeting, ids, source, excerpt, *, previous_role_evidence=None):
    ids = canonical_roster(ids)
    if any(not _name_present(excerpt, identifier) for identifier in ids):
        raise ValueError("Attendance excerpt does not support every normalized identity")
    # October 2026's resolution names attendees without repeating every role.
    # Carry only unchanged identities' prior explicitly documented role source;
    # do not reinterpret that source as a pre-cutoff appointment announcement.
    roles_explicit = all(role in excerpt for role in ("Governor", "Deputy Governor", "Executive Director"))
    members = []
    for identifier in ids:
        if roles_explicit:
            role_source, role_excerpt = source, excerpt
        else:
            if previous_role_evidence is None or identifier not in previous_role_evidence:
                raise ValueError("Role missing from attendance and no earlier documented role source")
            role_source, role_excerpt = previous_role_evidence[identifier]
        members.append(TemporalMember(member_id=identifier, name=MEMBERS[identifier][0],
                                      role=MEMBERS[identifier][1],
                                      is_internal=MEMBERS[identifier][1] != "External Member",
                                      role_evidence_source=role_source, role_evidence_excerpt=role_excerpt))
    members = tuple(members)
    governor = [m.member_id for m in members if m.role == "Governor"]
    if len(governor) != 1:
        raise ValueError("Attendance excerpt does not support exactly one known Governor")
    # The role labels must be present in the attendance text; external roles are
    # source-designated non-RBI members, not estimated behavioral preferences.
    return TemporalMeetingRoster(
        meeting_id=meeting["meeting_id"], decision_date=meeting["decision_date"],
        meeting_start_date=meeting["meeting_start_date"],
        information_cutoff=meeting["meeting_start_date"] + "T00:00:00+05:30",
        members=members, governor_id=governor[0], roster_source=source,
        roster_source_excerpt=excerpt)


def _original_inputs(store):
    meetings, statements = [], []
    directory = source_path(store.root, ORIGINAL / "2020-10-09/source_manifest.json").parent.parent
    for manifest_path in sorted(directory.glob("*/source_manifest.json")):
        relative = manifest_path.relative_to(store.root)
        store.read(relative)
        meta = _read_json(manifest_path)
        decision = meta["decision_date"]
        if manifest_path.parent.name != decision:
            raise ValueError("Original statement folder and decision disagree")
        source_id = Path(meta["source_file"]).stem
        prid = source_id.rsplit("_", 1)[-1]
        source = store.ref(meta["source_file"], meta["source_sha256"], source_id,
                           "https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=" + prid,
                           meta["publication_date"])
        soup = store.soups[meta["source_file"]]
        body = soup.select_one("#doublescroll")
        if body is None:
            raise ValueError("Missing official minutes article body")
        blocks = [normalized(e.get_text(" ", strip=True)) for e in body.find_all("p")]
        excerpts = [b for b in blocks if b.startswith("2.") and "meeting was attended" in b.lower()]
        if len(excerpts) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Ambiguous original attendance paragraph")
        meeting = {"meeting_id": "rbi_mpc_" + decision, "decision_date": decision,
                   "meeting_start_date": meta["meeting_start_date"]}
        roster = _roster(meeting, tuple(meta["statement_sha256"]), source, excerpts[0])
        meetings.append(roster)
        raw_text = normalized(soup.get_text())
        for old_id, digest in sorted(meta["statement_sha256"].items()):
            identifier = canonical_member_id(old_id)
            name = str(manifest_path.parent.relative_to(store.root) / (old_id + ".txt"))
            _, payload = store.read(name, digest)
            text = payload.decode("utf-8")
            if normalized(text) not in raw_text:
                raise ValueError("Personal statement is not in retained raw minutes")
            heading = _personal_heading(text, identifier)
            statements.append((PersonalStatementRef(
                statement_id=meeting["meeting_id"] + ":" + identifier, member_id=identifier,
                original_member_id=old_id, meeting_id=meeting["meeting_id"], decision_date=decision,
                source=source, statement_file=name, statement_sha256=digest,
                attribution_heading=heading), text))
    return meetings, statements


def _expanded_inputs(store):
    catalog_path, _ = store.read(EXPANDED / "source_catalog.json")
    ledger_path, _ = store.read(EXPANDED / "meeting_label_ledger.json")
    statement_path, _ = store.read(EXPANDED / "member_statements.jsonl")
    catalog = {r["source_id"]: r for r in _read_json(catalog_path)["records"]}
    ledger = _read_json(ledger_path)
    meetings, refs, prior_roles = [], {}, {}
    for row in ledger["meetings"]:
        evidence = row["roster_source_excerpt"]
        record = catalog[evidence["source_id"]]
        relative = EXPANDED / evidence["source_path"]
        if record["sha256"] != evidence["source_sha256"] or record["raw_path"] != evidence["source_path"]:
            raise ValueError("Roster source/catalog mismatch")
        source = store.ref(relative, record["sha256"], record["source_id"], record["url"],
                           record["publication_date"])
        if row["information_cutoff_exclusive_ist"] != row["meeting_start_date"] + "T00:00:00+05:30":
            raise ValueError("Expanded cutoff is inconsistent with meeting start")
"""Verify dated corpus bytes and fitted persona fields before research generation."""
import json
from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path

from src.infra.evidence import file_hash
from src.infra.exceptions import GenerationProvenanceError
from src.schemas.persona_schema import MemberPersona

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def verify_personas(personas, cutoff, *, source_root=None, corpus_manifest_path=None):
    root = Path(source_root or PROJECT_ROOT).resolve()
    if isinstance(cutoff, datetime):
        if cutoff.tzinfo is None:
            raise GenerationProvenanceError('Persona prediction cutoff needs a timezone')
        cutoff = cutoff.date().isoformat()
    if not isinstance(cutoff, str) or date.fromisoformat(cutoff).isoformat() != cutoff:
        raise GenerationProvenanceError('Persona prediction cutoff must be an ISO calendar day')
    validated = [MemberPersona.model_validate(p.model_dump()) for p in personas]
    if not validated or len({p.member_id for p in validated}) != len(validated):
        raise GenerationProvenanceError('Distinct nonempty research personas required')
    manifests = {}
    for persona in validated:
        if (persona.provenance_status != 'dated_corpus' or not persona.calibration_cutoff
                or persona.calibration_cutoff > cutoff):
            raise GenerationProvenanceError('Undated, assumed or future corpus cannot be research persona evidence')
        path = Path(corpus_manifest_path) if corpus_manifest_path else (
            root / 'personas' / f'calibration_{persona.calibration_cutoff}_v2' / 'corpus_manifest.json')
        if not path.is_file() or file_hash(path) != persona.corpus_manifest_hash:
            raise GenerationProvenanceError('Missing or changed persona corpus manifest')
        if path not in manifests:
            manifests[path] = json.loads(path.read_text())
        manifest = manifests[path]
        if manifest.get('calibration_cutoff') != persona.calibration_cutoff:
            raise GenerationProvenanceError('Persona and corpus cutoffs differ')
        member = manifest.get('members', {}).get(persona.member_id)
        if not member or not member.get('corpus_sources') or not member.get('meetings_count'):
            raise GenerationProvenanceError('Persona has no actual pre-cutoff corpus')
        fields = {'name': 'name', 'role': 'role', 'is_internal': 'is_internal',
                  'hawk_dove_score': 'calibrated_hawk_dove', 'stance_bias': 'stance_bias',
                  'voting_priority': 'voting_priority', 'biography': 'biography',
                  'key_themes': 'exemplar_quotes'}
        if any(getattr(persona, field) != member.get(key) for field, key in fields.items()):
            raise GenerationProvenanceError('Persona fields differ from their frozen corpus fit')
        if persona.system_prompt_override is not None:
            raise GenerationProvenanceError('An unregistered prompt override is not the frozen corpus fit')
        rows = member['corpus_sources']
        if len(rows) != member['meetings_count'] or len({r['decision_date'] for r in rows}) != len(rows):
            raise GenerationProvenanceError('Corpus source rows are duplicated or incomplete')
        for row in rows:
            decision = date.fromisoformat(row['decision_date']).isoformat()
            publication = date.fromisoformat(row['publication_date']).isoformat()
            if not decision <= publication < persona.calibration_cutoff:
                raise GenerationProvenanceError('Corpus statement is unavailable at calibration cutoff')
            for name in ('source', 'statement'):
                source = (root / row[f'{name}_file']).resolve()
                if (not source.is_relative_to(root) or not source.is_file()
                        or file_hash(source) != row[f'{name}_sha256']):
                    raise GenerationProvenanceError(f'Missing or changed persona {name} bytes')
    return validated

# Literature source register

Checked on 5 October 2026. This is a focused source/version register, not an exhaustive novelty search or independent replication of another paper's results.

## Kazinnik and Sinclair: FOMC In Silico

The [SSRN author record](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5424097) identifies a revision dated 12 July 2026, while retaining an original writing date of 31 August 2025. Its abstract reports a 218-meeting backtest through June 2026, 8.3 bps rate MAE and 91% hike/cut/hold accuracy. Those are author-reported results on a different committee and sample, not independently verified benchmarks for this project. The revised abstract describes deliberation as building consensus rather than improving forecasting.

The [GWU-hosted PDF](https://www2.gwu.edu/~forcpgm/2025-005.pdf) fetched during this check still opens with the August 2025 draft and July 2025 illustrative-meeting abstract. Its bytes differ from the bundled file: fetched SHA-256 `bb87d87e450d7a73206ab8845afc21d595dd6a3965c4a23b647f53f28ca70914`, bundled SHA-256 `e03bb52ccf932f4bfc25ddd2b0fb97e2458a67fb01fc91e396ecf705ab724209`. Different hashes establish different bytes, not the reason for the difference or a complete substantive revision comparison. Do not identify the bundled draft, current GWU bytes and revised SSRN abstract as the same verified version. The full revised SSRN manuscript has not been inspected here.

## Riboni and Ruge-Murcia (2010)

[Monetary policy by committee: Consensus, chairman dominance, or simple majority?](https://researchportal.ip-paris.fr/en/publications/monetary-policy-by-committee-consensus-chairman-dominance-or-simp/), *Quarterly Journal of Economics*, 125(1), 363-416. DOI: [10.1162/qjec.2010.125.1.363](https://doi.org/10.1162/qjec.2010.125.1.363).

The authors compare alternative committee decision models and estimate them against policy decisions. This provides a reason to examine voting and agenda assumptions rather than treating a chosen aggregation formula as a derived equilibrium. Applying a model's name does not transfer that paper's theoretical identification or empirical fit to another implementation.

Discovery used a fetched [Consensus record](https://consensus.app/papers/monetary-policy-by-committee-consensus-chairman-riboni-ruge-murcia/b5a2171ac973513a8c0b641211b48c91/?utm_source=chatgpt); publication metadata was checked against the author's institutional record above. Citation counts are provider-dependent and are not evidence of methodological correctness.

## Baerg and Lowe: textual preferences

[A textual Taylor rule: estimating central bank preferences combining topic and scaling methods](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/political-science-research-and-methods/article/abs/textual-taylor-rule-estimating-central-bank-preferences-combining-topic-and-scaling-methods/E1CAE25BBA2864109ACF25D599EDD083), *Political Science Research and Methods*, 8(1), January 2020, 106-122; published online 18 September 2018. DOI: [10.1017/psrm.2018.31](https://doi.org/10.1017/psrm.2018.31).

This work estimates preference measures from text through topic and scaling methods without defining them directly by voting outcomes. It is relevant to constructing and validating persona measures separately from the outcomes used to evaluate those personas. It does not validate an arbitrary dictionary score or mixture weight in this project.

The fetched [Consensus record](https://consensus.app/papers/a-textual-taylor-rule-estimating-central-bank-preferences-baerg-lowe/947ced3163f25134910e0b53a3d2df72/?utm_source=chatgpt) gave 2015 as its year; the primary publisher distinguishes the 2018 online date from the 2020 issue. Use the primary publication metadata in bibliographies.

  FOMC In Silico: A Multi-Agent System
 for Monetary Policy Decision Modeling

       This is a preliminary draft. The authors welcome all comments and suggestions.


                     Sophia Kazinnik∗                Tara M. Sinclair†
                                     August 31, 2025


                                           Abstract
        We develop a multi-agent framework for modeling the Federal Open Market
        Committee (FOMC) decision making process. The framework combines two
        approaches: an LLM-based simulation and a Monte Carlo implementation of
        a generalized Bayesian voting model. Both begin from identical prior beliefs
        about the appropriate interest rate for each committee member, formed using
        real-time data and member profiles. In a simulation replicating the July 2025
        FOMC meeting, both tracks deliver rates near the 4.25–4.50% range’s upper
        end (4.42% LLM, 4.38% MC). Political pressure scenario increases dissent
        and dispersion: the LLM track averages 4.38% and shows dissent in 88% of
        meetings; the MC track averages 4.39% and shows dissent in 61% of meetings.
        A negative jobs revision scenario moves outcomes lower: LLM at 4.30% (dissent
        in 74% of meeting), and MC at 4.32% (dissent in 62% of meeting), with final
        decisions remaining inside the 4.25-4.50% range. The framework isolates small,
        scenario-dependent wedges between behavioral and rational baselines, offering
        an in silico environment for counterfactual evaluation in monetary policy.


        Keywords: Generative AI; Multi-Agent Systems; Large Language Models,
        Federal Open Market Committee; Monetary Policy; Simulations

 1     Introduction
                                                   “Between the idea and the reality . . .
                                                   falls the shadow.”

                                                       T. S. Eliot, “The Hollow Men,”

    Monetary policy deliberations and the actual rate decision are separated by a
“shadow” of persuasion and norms. Decisions by the Federal Open Market Committee
(FOMC) reflect more than macroeconomic data and formal models; they also depend
on members’ experience, behavioral biases, and implicit rules (e.g., Hughes and
Fehrler, 2015; Haldane, 2018; Maih et al., 2021). Consequently, who participates in
the deliberation and how information is communicated can influence policy outcomes
beyond the underlying economic data.
    Precisely because of these behavioral forces, traditional models of committee
decision making, though useful and mathematically elegant, often miss the complex-
ities of real world interactions. Behavioral economics highlights how biases, well
documented by Tversky and Kahneman (1974) and shown to affect monetary policy
(Haldane, 2018), can systematically shape decisions. Information design matters too:
Bayesian persuasion demonstrates how agenda setters steer beliefs (Kamenica and
Gentzkow, 2011). Separately, robust control preferences reveal how officials facing
model uncertainty skew choices toward caution (Hansen and Sargent, 2008). Within
the FOMC, policy outcomes depend on the committee’s composition, from regional
voting rotation (e.g., Fos and Xu, 2025) to individual members’ policy leanings (e.g.,
Hack et al., 2023).
    To better capture such frictions, researchers increasingly use computational
approaches, such as agent-based models (Dwarakanath et al., 2024) and reinforcement
learning (Hinterlang and Tänzer, 2021). Large language models (LLMs) further
extend the frontier by enabling agents with coherent communication and emergent
behavior. LLM-based generative agents simulate realistic social interactions (Park

# Literature source register

Checked on 5 October 2026. This is a focused source/version register, not an exhaustive novelty search or independent replication of another paper's results.

## Kazinnik and Sinclair: FOMC In Silico

The [SSRN author record](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5424097) identifies a revision dated 12 July 2026, while retaining an original writing date of 31 August 2025. Its abstract reports a 218-meeting backtest through June 2026, 8.3 bps rate MAE and 91% hike/cut/hold accuracy. Those are author-reported results on a different committee and sample, not independently verified benchmarks for this project. The revised abstract describes deliberation as building consensus rather than improving forecasting.

The [GWU-hosted PDF](https://www2.gwu.edu/~forcpgm/2025-005.pdf) fetched during this check still opens with the August 2025 draft and July 2025 illustrative-meeting abstract. Its bytes differ from the bundled file: fetched SHA-256 `bb87d87e450d7a73206ab8845afc21d595dd6a3965c4a23b647f53f28ca70914`, bundled SHA-256 `e03bb52ccf932f4bfc25ddd2b0fb97e2458a67fb01fc91e396ecf705ab724209`. Different hashes establish different bytes, not the reason for the difference or a complete substantive revision comparison. Do not identify the bundled draft, current GWU bytes and revised SSRN abstract as the same verified version. The full revised SSRN manuscript has not been inspected here.

## Riboni and Ruge-Murcia (2010)

[Monetary policy by committee: Consensus, chairman dominance, or simple majority?](https://researchportal.ip-paris.fr/en/publications/monetary-policy-by-committee-consensus-chairman-dominance-or-simp/), *Quarterly Journal of Economics*, 125(1), 363-416. DOI: [10.1162/qjec.2010.125.1.363](https://doi.org/10.1162/qjec.2010.125.1.363).

The authors compare alternative committee decision models and estimate them against policy decisions. This provides a reason to examine voting and agenda assumptions rather than treating a chosen aggregation formula as a derived equilibrium. Applying a model's name does not transfer that paper's theoretical identification or empirical fit to another implementation.

Discovery used a fetched [Consensus record](https://consensus.app/papers/monetary-policy-by-committee-consensus-chairman-riboni-ruge-murcia/b5a2171ac973513a8c0b641211b48c91/?utm_source=chatgpt); publication metadata was checked against the author's institutional record above. Citation counts are provider-dependent and are not evidence of methodological correctness.

## Baerg and Lowe: textual preferences

[A textual Taylor rule: estimating central bank preferences combining topic and scaling methods](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/political-science-research-and-methods/article/abs/textual-taylor-rule-estimating-central-bank-preferences-combining-topic-and-scaling-methods/E1CAE25BBA2864109ACF25D599EDD083), *Political Science Research and Methods*, 8(1), January 2020, 106-122; published online 18 September 2018. DOI: [10.1017/psrm.2018.31](https://doi.org/10.1017/psrm.2018.31).

This work estimates preference measures from text through topic and scaling methods without defining them directly by voting outcomes. It is relevant to constructing and validating persona measures separately from the outcomes used to evaluate those personas. It does not validate an arbitrary dictionary score or mixture weight in this project.

The fetched [Consensus record](https://consensus.app/papers/a-textual-taylor-rule-estimating-central-bank-preferences-baerg-lowe/947ced3163f25134910e0b53a3d2df72/?utm_source=chatgpt) gave 2015 as its year; the primary publisher distinguishes the 2018 online date from the 2020 issue. # Source-linked original historical labels

These inputs describe the 25 already exposed RBI MPC decisions from 9 October 2020 to 8 August 2024. They are retrospective scientific data. Reconstruction or repeated inspection does not make this panel an untouched evaluation.

`label_annotations.json` retains the scientific interpretation fields, committee-resolution excerpts, publication/decision/start dates, source paths and raw-source SHA-256 identities. Its provenance records the SHA-256 of the archival scientific truth from which the interpretation fields were exported. Every retained excerpt was checked against the corresponding primary-source bytes. This is a portable annotation export, not independent second coding. No numerical rate or stance outcome is imported from the legacy parquet.

`label_ledger.json` adds the published repo level before/after each meeting, the rate change derived from consecutive levels, the stance category derived from the committee's published clause, and the six literal rate-ballot cells. Source dates, selected clauses, rate ballots and attributed signed-statement votes are checked during every reconstruction. The complete April/May 2022 clause remains available: the committee remained accommodative while focusing on withdrawal of accommodation; the leading published category is `accommodative`.

`observed_targets.json` exposes chronological `{meeting_date, member_targets:{member_id:bool|null}}` records separately for literal rate No, disagreement with the committee's exact rate quantum, and formal stance dissent. For this original panel, the two rate channels both contain 150 observed targets, including ten positive events. They are separate definitions even though their targets coincide here. A No vote against a quantified resolution establishes disagreement; it does not identify every alternative magnitude. Narrative preferences that ultimately concur with the binding resolution are not relabeled as formal dissent.

Formal stance contains 144 observed targets, fifteen positives and six missing targets. Nineteen meetings have complete stance labels. Jayanth Varma's reservations in August 2022 and April, June, August, October and December 2023 remain `null`. The four reservations in the 2021–February 2022 committee summaries are resolved by an attributed, explicit signed-statement vote against the stance. The October 2020 disagreement over the duration/formulation of forward guidance stays separate from the accommodative stance category. Missingness never means a known negative, affirmative ballot or invented abstention.

`input_manifest.json` freezes the SHA-256 of 122 required scientific files: these annotations/labels/targets, the observation ledgers, 25 original minutes, the prior policy resolution/record, and the retained CPI, GDP/GVA and FOMC raw sources used by those ledgers. A separately retained manifest digest can anchor a copied source root:

```
0c618df1e00a4731c9a312799a65c472d1d5e6815bff4f19a66b2430de4cd757
```

From the project root, one offline command builds the scientific panel and labels into an explicit new destination:

```sh
.venv/bin/python research/verification/rebuild_scientific_inputs.py \
  --source-root . \
  --output-root /absolute/path/to/new-reconstruction \
  --expected-input-manifest-sha256 0c618df1e00a4731c9a312799a65c472d1d5e6815bff4f19a66b2430de4cd757
```

It writes `panel/{snapshots,truth,manifest}.json`, `labels/{label_ledger,observed_targets}.json` and `reconstruction_receipt.json`. The receipt records input hashes, code identity, runtime/dependency details and zero network/model calls. An optional `--reference-panel data/processed/vintage_v3` records byte and semantic comparisons; the reference is not used to construct scientific inputs. The rebuilt snapshots and archival truth are byte identical to `vintage_v3`; the manifest differs in its version and added label-ledger/input-manifest/observability metadata. Archival truth preserves known-positive lists for old-study replay. New observability-aware scoring must use the explicit member targets rather than interpreting a missing formal vote as a negative.

The standalone export command consumes only these annotations and retained primary sources:

```sh
.venv/bin/python research/source_ledgers/historical_labels_round002/export_labels.py \
  --source-root . --output-dir /absolute/path/to/new-label-export
```

Preserve the catalogue and source bytes as one scientific version. A new input version needs its own declared catalogue and outputs. A checksum ties transcriptions to retained bytes; it does not authenticate contemporaneous web availability or prove that no intermediate revision existed. Missing output gap, core/food CPI, IIP, liquidity, FX, oil and monsoon inputs stay missing. Engineering reconstruction is not empirical model replication, forecasting skill, cognitive diversity or causal policy evidence.

For a source-only scientific copy, include `src/`, this whole directory, `research/verification/rebuild_scientific_inputs.py`, `research/source_ledgers/prior_policy/`, all observation ledger/raw files named in `input_manifest.json`, and the 25 `data/raw/minutes_html/` files named there. `data/processed/macro_panel.parquet`, audit results, Git history, model credentials and prior assessments are unnecessary. Tests may additionally include `tests/test_vintage_rebuild.py` and archival `data/processed/vintage_v3/` for the optional equivalence check.
# Source-label reconciliation

The two retained source passes were written separately. This directory compares them and records parent adjudication; it does not call the result independent consensus or a universal gold standard. Neither model predictions nor prior forecasting scores entered these decisions.

Both passes agree on all 78 exact rate choices and rate-choice disagreements. Literal ballot agreement includes six unknown cells; only 72 literal ballots are observed. Three literal No ballots differ from four exact-magnitude disagreements because June 2025 Bhattacharya votes Yes for a 25-bps cut while the committee chooses 50 bps.

For formal stance, 76 of 78 entries agree including unknowns. Two personal statements explicitly link a status-quo vote to both rate and stance. The primary definition accepts these contextual personal votes as neutral, with the preceding neutral stance as referent. A strict-narrative sensitivity preserves the second coder's nulls. Both original annotations, excerpts and reasons remain in comparison.json. Resolution-reported October 2026 preferences are not substituted for unavailable personal statements.

The primary definition observes 20 formal stance cells; the strict sensitivity observes 18. Only three meetings have all six stance votes observed. Unknown votes, unassessed reservations and unassessed guidance are never coded as negatives. These labels cover an already exposed retrospective panel of 13 decisions, including eight holds, four cuts and one increase. `calibrated_tightening` is outside the current simulator's three-stance ontology and requires explicit versioned integration.

`build_adjudication.py` verifies 25 shared primary-source hashes and 386 exact annotation raw fragments, then writes new outputs exclusively. The independent pass's broader annotations-plus-statements check covers 1,048 fragments separately; these counts refer to different inputs. Hashes check retained consistency, not authenticated historical first availability.

`evaluate_missing_labels.py` produces one offline no-dissent baseline diagnostic for each distinct channel, including the strict stance sensitivity. The new evaluator reports observed and complete cases plus sharp logical bounds over every possible assignment to missing labels. Bounds are not confidence intervals and do not assume random missingness. This deterministic baseline uses no model generation and cannot establish model performance. Run into a new output directory:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python research/source_ledgers/expanded_panel_oct09_adjudication/evaluate_missing_labels.py --output-dir results/source_label_diagnostics_new
```

"""Strong, reproducible historical baselines; only published prior truth is usable."""
from collections import Counter
from datetime import date
import hashlib
import json
from src.validation.metrics import MetricsEvaluator


def fit_dissent_baseline(calibration_truth, cutoff="2023-04-06", *, information_cutoff="2023-04-30"):
    if date.fromisoformat(cutoff).isoformat() != cutoff or date.fromisoformat(information_cutoff).isoformat() != information_cutoff:
        raise ValueError('Baseline cutoffs must be ISO calendar dates')
    if not calibration_truth or any(row['meeting_date'] > cutoff for row in calibration_truth):
        raise ValueError('Holdout or empty truth in calibration')
    if len({row['meeting_date'] for row in calibration_truth}) != len(calibration_truth):
        raise ValueError('Duplicate calibration meeting')
    for row in calibration_truth:
        meeting, publication = date.fromisoformat(row['meeting_date']), date.fromisoformat(row['publication_date'])
        if publication < meeting or row['publication_date'] >= information_cutoff:
            raise ValueError('Calibration labels are unavailable at the declared selection freeze')
    result = {'cutoff': cutoff, 'information_cutoff':information_cutoff,
              'method': 'best constant dissent set per channel by calibration F1 then exact-match',
              'selection_status': 'calibration only; cohort-specific',
              'calibration_hash': hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(calibration_truth, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()}
    for channel in ('rate_dissenters', 'stance_dissenters'):
        candidates = sorted({tuple(sorted(row[channel])) for row in calibration_truth})
        truth = [row[channel] for row in calibration_truth]
        scored = []
        for candidate in candidates:
            precision, recall, f1, exact = MetricsEvaluator.compute_dissent_f1([candidate] * len(truth), truth)
            scored.append((f1 if f1 is not None else -1, exact, candidate))
        # Lexical tie-break is predetermined and recorded; no evaluation labels used.
        result[channel] = list(max(scored, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1], tuple(item[2])))[2])
    return result


def baseline_predictions(snapshots, truth, frozen_dissent):
    by_date = {row['meeting_date']: row for row in truth}
    if len(by_date) != len(truth):
        raise ValueError('Duplicate truth meeting')
    rows = []
    for snapshot in snapshots:
        # Entire minutes publication day precedes the meeting-start cutoff.
        cutoff = snapshot.information_cutoff.date().isoformat() if snapshot.information_cutoff else snapshot.meeting_date
        available = sorted([r for r in truth if r['publication_date'] < cutoff], key=lambda r:r['meeting_date'])
        prior = available[-1] if available else None
        for name in ('hold_previous_stance', 'lag_persistence', 'calibration_constant_dissent'):
            rate = prior['actual_rate_bps'] if name == 'lag_persistence' and prior else 0
            stance = prior['actual_stance'] if name == 'lag_persistence' and prior else snapshot.prev_stance
            rate_dissent = prior['rate_dissenters'] if name == 'lag_persistence' and prior else []
            stance_dissent = prior['stance_dissenters'] if name == 'lag_persistence' and prior else []
            if name == 'calibration_constant_dissent':
                if snapshot.meeting_date <= frozen_dissent['cutoff'] or cutoff < frozen_dissent['information_cutoff']:
                    raise ValueError('Fitted baseline evaluated inside calibration')
                rate_dissent, stance_dissent = frozen_dissent['rate_dissenters'], frozen_dissent['stance_dissenters']
            rows.append({'meeting_date':snapshot.meeting_date, 'baseline':name, 'rate_bps':rate,
                         'stance':stance, 'rate_dissenters':list(rate_dissent), 'stance_dissenters':list(stance_dissent),
                         'source_prior_meeting':prior['meeting_date'] if prior else None,
                         'evidence_type':'deterministic_baseline'})
    return rows

"""Semantic validation of copied generation evidence, beyond content digests.

Digests detect accidental changes; they do not authenticate a provider invoice.
Replay must also reconcile the recorded schema, request, evidence track and cost.
"""

import json
import math
from datetime import date, datetime

from src.infra.cost_governor import PRICE_REVISION, PRICE_SOURCE, TOKEN_RATES_PER_MILLION
from src.infra.evidence import canonical_json, content_hash
from src.infra.exceptions import ArtifactIntegrityError, GenerationProvenanceError

REQUIRED_METADATA_FIELDS = frozenset("""
request_id request_hash request_payload_json provider requested_model routed_model served_model model_epoch
response_id seed provider_reported_seed temperature max_output_tokens input_token_bound input_bound_method
schema_name schema_hash schema_json parser_version prompt_hash system_prompt user_prompt cache_key cache_replay
source_request_id source_evidence_type evidence_type attempt_count finish_reason input_tokens output_tokens
token_usage_source estimated_cost_usd reservation_id price_revision price_source created_at
""".split())


def strict_json(text: str):
    def unique(pairs):
        result = {}
        for key, value in pairs:
            if key in result:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate JSON field {key!r}")
            result[key] = value
        return result

    def finite(value):
        raise ValueError(f"Nonfinite JSON value {value}")

    value = json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=unique, parse_constant=finite)
    canonical_json(value)  # Also rejects overflow such as 1e999.
    return value


def validate_recorded_schema(value, schema: dict, *, schema_only: bool = False) -> None:
    """Use the actual recorded schema, with strict integers and no remote fetching."""
    try:
        from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator, validators
        from jsonschema.exceptions import SchemaError, ValidationError
        from referencing import Registry
        from referencing.exceptions import NoSuchResource, Unresolvable
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ArtifactIntegrityError("jsonschema dependency is required to validate replay evidence") from exc

    def no_remote(uri):
        raise NoSuchResource(ref=uri)

    def check_references(node):
        if isinstance(node, dict):
            for key, child in node.items():
                if key in {"$ref", "$dynamicRef"} and (not isinstance(child, str) or not child.startswith("#")):
                    raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Recorded schema may not fetch external references")
                check_references(child)
        elif isinstance(node, list):
            for child in node:
                check_references(child)

    try:
        check_references(schema)
        Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)
        checker = Draft202012Validator.TYPE_CHECKER.redefine(
            "integer", lambda _, item: type(item) is int,
        ).redefine("number", lambda _, item: type(item) is int or type(item) is float and math.isfinite(item))
        validator = validators.extend(Draft202012Validator, type_checker=checker)
        if not schema_only:
            validator(schema, registry=Registry(retrieve=no_remote)).validate(value)
    except (SchemaError, ValidationError, Unresolvable, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise ArtifactIntegrityError(f"Output violates recorded strict schema: {exc}") from exc


def validate_generation_evidence(generation: dict, *, identity_aliases: dict | None = None) -> dict | None:
    """Reject semantic contradictions in a successful generation/cache/replay record."""
    try:
        canonical_json(generation)
        metadata = generation["metadata"]
        if not isinstance(metadata, dict) or set(metadata) != REQUIRED_METADATA_FIELDS:
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Generation metadata is incomplete or has unknown fields")
        request = strict_json(metadata["request_payload_json"])
        identity = generation["request_identity"]
        if not isinstance(identity, dict) or request["request_identity"] != identity:
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Canonical generation identity differs from the request")
        if metadata["request_hash"] != content_hash(request) or metadata["cache_key"] != metadata["request_hash"]:
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Generation request hash mismatch")
        for field in ("provider", "routed_model", "temperature", "seed", "max_output_tokens", "model_epoch",
                      "parser_version", "system_prompt", "user_prompt"):
            if request[field] != metadata[field] or type(request[field]) is not type(metadata[field]):
                raise ArtifactIntegrityError(f"Generation {field} differs from canonical request")
        if metadata["requested_model"] != metadata["routed_model"]:
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Unexpected model substitution in generation evidence")
        schema = request["schema"]
        if metadata["schema_hash"] != content_hash(schema) or strict_json(metadata["schema_json"]) != schema:
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Generation schema provenance differs from request")
        if metadata["prompt_hash"] != content_hash({"system": request["system_prompt"], "user": request["user_prompt"]}):
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Generation prompt hash mismatch")
        if type(metadata["seed"]) is not int or type(metadata["attempt_count"]) is not int or metadata["attempt_count"] != 1:
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Generation seed/attempt count is invalid")
        if type(metadata["temperature"]) not in (float, int) or not 0 <= metadata["temperature"] <= 2:
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Generation temperature is invalid")
        for field, minimum in (("input_token_bound", 0), ("max_output_tokens", 1), ("input_tokens", 0), ("output_tokens", 0)):
            if type(metadata[field]) is not int or metadata[field] < minimum:
                raise ArtifactIntegrityError(f"Generation {field} is missing or invalid")
        if metadata["input_token_bound"] != request["generation_config"]["input_token_bound"]:
            raise ArtifactIntegrityError("Generation input reservation differs from request")
        if request["generation_config"] != {"response_mime_type": "application/json", "candidate_count": 1,

"""Reconstruct the original historical scientific panel entirely offline.

Invoke from a source-only checkout with an explicit new output root. Comparisons
against an archival panel are optional diagnostics, never reconstruction inputs.
"""
import argparse
import importlib.metadata
import json
import platform
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
from src.data_pipeline.vintage_panel import (LABEL_DIRECTORY, build_vintage_panel, digest,
                                            read_json, source_path, verify_input_manifest, write_new)
from research.source_ledgers.historical_labels_round002.export_labels import export


def rebuild_scientific_inputs(source_root, output_root, *, expected_input_manifest_sha256=None,
                              reference_panel=None):
    root = Path(source_root).resolve()
    output = Path(output_root).resolve()
    if output.exists():
        raise FileExistsError("Use a new output root; reconstruction never overwrites an existing artifact")
    if output == root or root.is_relative_to(output):
        raise ValueError("Output root cannot contain the scientific source root")
    input_manifest_path = source_path(root, LABEL_DIRECTORY / "input_manifest.json")
    input_manifest_hash = digest(input_manifest_path)
    if expected_input_manifest_sha256 is not None and expected_input_manifest_sha256 != input_manifest_hash:
        raise ValueError("Separately supplied scientific input manifest anchor does not match")
    catalog = verify_input_manifest(root)
    # These are the actual numerical reconstruction dependencies, not code history.
    code_paths = ("src/data_pipeline/vintage_panel.py", "src/data_pipeline/statement_extractor.py",
                  "src/schemas/macro_schema.py", "src/schemas/decision_space.py",
                  "research/source_ledgers/historical_labels_round002/export_labels.py",
                  "research/verification/rebuild_scientific_inputs.py")
    code_hashes = {name: digest(source_path(root, name)) for name in code_paths}
    build_vintage_panel(output / "panel", gdp_ledger="research/source_ledgers/gdp_fed_vintages/meeting_gdp_ledger.csv",
                        source_root=root)
    export(root, output / "labels")
    if catalog != verify_input_manifest(root) or digest(input_manifest_path) != input_manifest_hash:
        raise ValueError("Scientific inputs changed during offline reconstruction")
    if any(digest(source_path(root, name)) != sha for name, sha in code_hashes.items()):
        raise ValueError("Scientific reconstruction code changed during execution")
    comparisons = {}
    if reference_panel is not None:
        reference = Path(reference_panel).resolve()
        for name in ("snapshots.json", "truth.json", "manifest.json"):
            original, rebuilt = reference / name, output / "panel" / name
            before, after = read_json(original), read_json(rebuilt)
            comparisons[name] = {"reference_sha256": digest(original), "rebuilt_sha256": digest(rebuilt),
                                 "byte_equal": original.read_bytes() == rebuilt.read_bytes(),
                                 "semantic_equal": before == after}
            if name == "manifest.json":
                comparisons[name]["different_keys"] = sorted(key for key in set(before) | set(after)
                                                             if before.get(key) != after.get(key))
    versions = {name: importlib.metadata.version(name) for name in ("pydantic", "beautifulsoup4")}
    receipt = {"version": "offline-historical-input-reconstruction-v1", "status": "complete",
               "input_manifest_sha256": input_manifest_hash, "scientific_input_files": len(catalog["files"]),
               "input_hashes": catalog["files"], "code_sha256": code_hashes,
               "environment": {"python": sys.version, "executable": sys.executable,
                               "platform": platform.platform(), "dependencies": versions},
               "command_arguments": sys.argv, "reference_comparison": comparisons,
               "reference_used_for_construction": False, "network_calls": 0, "model_calls": 0,
               "scope": "Source reconstruction and observability, not empirical model replication or superiority"}
    write_new(output / "reconstruction_receipt.json", receipt)
    return receipt


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--source-root", type=Path, default=ROOT)
    parser.add_argument("--output-root", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-input-manifest-sha256")
    parser.add_argument("--reference-panel", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = rebuild_scientific_inputs(args.source_root, args.output_root,
                                      expected_input_manifest_sha256=args.expected_input_manifest_sha256,
                                      reference_panel=args.reference_panel)
    print(json.dumps({"status": result["status"], "scientific_input_files": result["scientific_input_files"],
                      "reference_comparison": result["reference_comparison"]}, sort_keys=True))

"""Canonical, finite, immutable evidence helpers shared by runtime components."""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from src.infra.exceptions import ArtifactIntegrityError, GenerationProvenanceError


def canonical_json(value: Any) -> str:
    try:
        return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
                          ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise GenerationProvenanceError("Evidence must be finite JSON") from exc


def content_hash(value: Any) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_json(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def file_hash(path: str | Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with Path(path).open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def safe_component(value: Any) -> str:
    component = str(value)
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*", component) or component in {".", ".."}:
        raise GenerationProvenanceError(f"Unsafe artifact path component: {component!r}")
    return component


def write_immutable(path: str | Path, value: Any, *, replay: bool = False) -> Path:
    """Publish fsynced canonical bytes without replacing an existing artifact."""
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    raw = (canonical_json(value) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    descriptor, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".evidence-", dir=path.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(raw)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        try:
            # A hard link publishes complete bytes atomically and fails on collisions.
            os.link(temporary, path)
        except FileExistsError as exc:
            if not replay or path.read_bytes() != raw:
                raise ArtifactIntegrityError(f"Immutable artifact already exists: {path}") from exc
        directory = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY)
        try:
            os.fsync(directory)
        finally:
            os.close(directory)
    finally:
        os.unlink(temporary)
    return path

"""Strong, reproducible historical baselines; only published prior truth is usable."""
from collections import Counter
from datetime import date
import hashlib
import json
from src.validation.metrics import MetricsEvaluator


def fit_dissent_baseline(calibration_truth, cutoff="2023-04-06", *, information_cutoff="2023-04-30"):
    if date.fromisoformat(cutoff).isoformat() != cutoff or date.fromisoformat(information_cutoff).isoformat() != information_cutoff:
        raise ValueError('Baseline cutoffs must be ISO calendar dates')
    if not calibration_truth or any(row['meeting_date'] > cutoff for row in calibration_truth):
        raise ValueError('Holdout or empty truth in calibration')
    if len({row['meeting_date'] for row in calibration_truth}) != len(calibration_truth):
        raise ValueError('Duplicate calibration meeting')
    for row in calibration_truth:
        meeting, publication = date.fromisoformat(row['meeting_date']), date.fromisoformat(row['publication_date'])
        if publication < meeting or row['publication_date'] >= information_cutoff:
            raise ValueError('Calibration labels are unavailable at the declared selection freeze')
    result = {'cutoff': cutoff, 'information_cutoff':information_cutoff,
              'method': 'best constant dissent set per channel by calibration F1 then exact-match',
              'selection_status': 'calibration only; cohort-specific',
              'calibration_hash': hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(calibration_truth, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()}
    for channel in ('rate_dissenters', 'stance_dissenters'):
        candidates = sorted({tuple(sorted(row[channel])) for row in calibration_truth})
        truth = [row[channel] for row in calibration_truth]
        scored = []
        for candidate in candidates:
            precision, recall, f1, exact = MetricsEvaluator.compute_dissent_f1([candidate] * len(truth), truth)
            scored.append((f1 if f1 is not None else -1, exact, candidate))
        # Lexical tie-break is predetermined and recorded; no evaluation labels used.
        result[channel] = list(max(scored, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1], tuple(item[2])))[2])
    return result


def baseline_predictions(snapshots, truth, frozen_dissent):
    by_date = {row['meeting_date']: row for row in truth}
    if len(by_date) != len(truth):
        raise ValueError('Duplicate truth meeting')
    rows = []
    for snapshot in snapshots:
        # Entire minutes publication day precedes the meeting-start cutoff.
        cutoff = snapshot.information_cutoff.date().isoformat() if snapshot.information_cutoff else snapshot.meeting_date
        available = sorted([r for r in truth if r['publication_date'] < cutoff], key=lambda r:r['meeting_date'])
        prior = available[-1] if available else None
        for name in ('hold_previous_stance', 'lag_persistence', 'calibration_constant_dissent'):
            rate = prior['actual_rate_bps'] if name == 'lag_persistence' and prior else 0
            stance = prior['actual_stance'] if name == 'lag_persistence' and prior else snapshot.prev_stance
            rate_dissent = prior['rate_dissenters'] if name == 'lag_persistence' and prior else []
            stance_dissent = prior['stance_dissenters'] if name == 'lag_persistence' and prior else []
            if name == 'calibration_constant_dissent':
                if snapshot.meeting_date <= frozen_dissent['cutoff'] or cutoff < frozen_dissent['information_cutoff']:

                rate_dissent, stance_dissent = frozen_dissent['rate_dissenters'], frozen_dissent['stance_dissenters']

Varma 48. In the last several meetings, my statements have expressed the belief that the balance of risk and reward is in favour of monetary accommodation. As the pandemic continues to mutate, it appears to me that the balance of risk and reward is gradually shifting, and this merits a hard look at the accommodative stance. 49. First, Covid-19 is beginning to look more and more like tuberculosis which kills a very large number of people every year without inflicting major damage to the economy; in other words, it is beginning to resemble a neutron bomb. The ability of monetary policy to mitigate a human tragedy of this nature is very limited as compared to its ability to contain an economic crisis. Related to this is the lengthening of the time horizon of the pandemic. Global experience (particularly countries like Israel which are witnessing rising case counts despite very high levels of vaccination) suggests that vaccination is insufficient to stamp out the pandemic though it might reduce its severity. The possibility that Covid-19 will haunt us (though with lower mortality) for the next 3-5 years can no longer be ruled out. Keeping monetary policy highly accommodative for such a long horizon is very different from doing so for what was earlier expected to be a relatively short crisis. 50. Second, monetary policy has very broad effects on the entire economy, and this was appropriate in the early phase of the pandemic which caused generalized economic distress. More recently, however, the ill effects of the pandemic have been concentrated in narrow pockets of the economy. At the industry level, contact intensive services have suffered heavily, while many other industries are now operating above pre-Covid levels. At the firm level, MSMEs have suffered severely, while large businesses have prospered. At the household level, the pandemic has been devastating for weaker sections of the society, while the affluent have weathered it reasonably well. Geographically also, the pandemic has done its worst damage in around 100-200 districts spread across a relatively small number of states. Monetary policy is much less effective than fiscal policy for providing targeted relief to the worst affected segments of the economy. Indeed, monetary accommodation appears to be stimulating asset price inflation to a greater extent than it is mitigating the distress in the economy. 51. Third, inflationary pressures are beginning to show signs of greater persistence than anticipated earlier. There are indications that inflationary expectations may be becoming more widely entrenched. Most worrying of all, there is now a reduced degree of confidence that demand side inflationary pressures would remain quiescent. After averaging above 6% in 2020-21, inflation is forecast to be well above 5% in 2021-22, and is not expected to drop below 5% even in the first quarter of 2022-23 according to RBI projections. While there is some comfort that inflation is forecast to be below the upper end of the tolerance band, it is important to emphasize that the inflation target for the MPC is 4% and not 6% or even 5%. The tolerance band is designed to allow for forecast errors, implementation shortfalls and measurement issues. Treating 5% as the target would significantly increase the risk of inflation targeting failures. (While I have seen some commentary suggesting that there may be a case for raising the inflation target during the pandemic, that decision clearly lies with the government and not with the MPC.) 52. In this context, I believe that the current level of the reverse repo rate is no longer appropriate. I am conscious of the fact that the MPC’s mandate is supposed to be restricted to the policy rate or the repo rate. Unfortunately, the monetary policy statement of this meeting (as in the past several meetings) contains the line: “Consequently, the reverse repo rate under the LAF remains unchanged at 3.35 per cent”. I have for some time now being arguing that if the reverse repo rate does not fall within the remit of the MPC, then the announcement of this rate should be in the Governor’s statement and not in the MPC’s statement, but this view has not found favour with the rest of the MPC. Hence, I have no choice but to express my disagreement with the level of the reverse repo rate. A gradual normalization of the width of the corridor is warranted. In my view, a phased normalization of the corridor would increase the ability of the MPC to keep the repo rate at 4% for a longer period, and this should in my view be a greater priority for the MPC than maintaining an ultra-low reverse repo rate for some more time. 53. At a time when the economic recovery is still nascent, it is extremely important that monetary policy serves as an anchor of macroeconomic stability. That would reduce the inflation risk premium as well as the term premium and help stabilize long term interest rates. As I have argued in my past statements, a low long term interest rate is more important for inducing an investment led growth than a low short term rate. In this light, I fear that the forward guidance and monetary stance are becoming counter productive. By creating the erroneous perception that the MPC is no longer concerned about inflation and is focused exclusively on growth, the MPC may be inadvertently aggravating the risk that inflationary expectations will be disanchored. In that scenario, rising risk premia could cause long term rates to rise. Easy money today could lead to high interest rates tomorrow. On the other hand, by demonstrating its commitment to the inflation target with tangible action, the MPC will be able to anchor expectations, reduce risk premia, and sustain lower long term interest rates for longer thereby aiding the economic recovery. For these reasons, I am not in favour of the decision to keep the reverse repo rate at 3.35%, and vote against the accommodative stance. 54. On the other hand, I vote for maintaining the repo rate at 4% for the following reasons. Economic growth was unsatisfactory long before the pandemic, and even if the economic ill effects of the pandemic abate to some extent, substantial monetary accommodation is warranted. Persistent high inflation means that the monetary accommodation has to be somewhat restrained, and, therefore, I argued above for raising money market rates towards the repo rate of 4% from the current ultra-low level of 3.35%. The repo rate of 4% corresponds to a negative real rate in the range of 1-1.5% based on forward looking inflation forecasts. In my view, this level of rates is currently appropriate for reviving economic growth without excessive risk of an inflationary spiral. Needless to say, the MPC needs to remain data driven so that it can respond rapidly and adequately to any unforeseen shocks that may arise in future.Statement by Prof. Jayanth R. Varma 40. Inflation is at unacceptably high levels, and the projected trajectory is also above target during the entire forecast horizon. Economic growth has on the other hand proved resilient in the face of an adverse global environment. In this situation, there is clearly a need for front loaded hikes in the policy rate. The choice to my mind is between 50, 60 and 75 basis points. 41. The logic of front loading argues in favour of a 75 basis point hike: it would establish the credibility of monetary policy beyond doubt, would help achieve a faster reduction in the inflation rate, and would hopefully reduce the terminal repo rate consistent with bringing inflation close to the target. Weighing against that is the fact that a 75 basis point rate hike is quite unusual (despite a few recent hikes of this magnitude globally in the recent period). In the context of market expectations of a 35-50 basis point hike, such a large hike risks being misinterpreted as a sign of panic, and could be unnecessarily disruptive. Also even with a 50 basis point hike this month, the cumulative tightening in the past few months of 140 basis points would make the real interest rate positive based on projected inflation 3-4 quarters ahead. On balance, therefore, I do not favour a 75 basis point hike at this juncture. 42. The choice between 50 and 60 basis points is less clear cut. The latter has the advantage of bringing the repo rate back to a round multiple of a quarter percent, but shares some of the disadvantage of a 75 basis point hike to a much lesser extent. As I have argued in past statements, 10 basis points is not material and I am happy to go along with the consensus of the rest of the MPC on this issue. Therefore, I vote in favour of increasing the policy repo rate by 50 basis points to 5.40 per cent. 43. I now turn to the second resolution to remain focused on withdrawal of accommodation to ensure that inflation remains within the target going forward, while supporting growth. This statement confuses more than it clarifies. Because the rate hike in this meeting takes the policy rate above the pre-pandemic level, “withdrawal of accommodation” cannot refer to the withdrawal of the pandemic era accommodation. It can only mean withdrawal of the pre-pandemic accommodation that began with the rate cut from 6.50% to 6.25% in February 2019. A plain reading of this resolution would then be that the MPC is focused on taking the repo rate back to 6.50%. 44. In my view, such an indication of a terminal repo rate of 6.50% is totally unwarranted in the situation that we are in. The reality is that the Ukraine war and monetary tightening in the advanced economies have led to a very serious risk of recession in the world economy. In the face of this, commodity prices have collapsed from their April peaks. Crude oil remained elevated for longer, but it too is softening even as the MPC meeting is in progress. If this trend continues, we could see significant downward adjustments to the projected inflation trajectory. Moreover, though the Indian economy has been highly resilient to geopolitical and commodity price shocks so far, the weakening of exports in July indicates that India would not be immune to growth shocks emanating from the rest of the world. In short, it is easy to imagine that a few months from now, the economic data could point to a terminal repo rate that is well below 6.50%. To focus on one thing implies paying less attention to other things, and I do not think it would be wise to say that the MPC will remain “focused” on withdrawal of accommodation ignoring other considerations. 45. I have made several different suggestions to the MPC regarding alternatives to this resolution. First, in June, I suggested that individual MPC members could start moving towards providing projections of the future path of the policy rate. Since these would be projections of individual members and not of the MPC as a whole, these projections would not tie the hands of the MPC itself in any way. At the same time, they would provide guidance to the public about the thinking within the MPC. Second, at this meeting, I suggested that this resolution should simply be dropped. It is better not to give any guidance than to give confusing guidance. Unfortunately, none of these proposals found favour with the other members. 46. At the same time, I do not wish to record an outright dissent on this resolution because clearly further withdrawal of accommodation is warranted. The terminal repo rate may or may not be 6.50% but it is almost certainly well above 5.40%. So I am confining myself to expressing my reservations on this resolution. The resolution should in my view be interpreted only as stating that there is a high likelihood of further front-loaded tightening without restricting the freedom of the MPC to respond to the changing environment in a data driven manner.45ZI.
